Of course, there could be optimizations to make it more efficient. But proofing state, logs, eth_call, etc. together with efficient consensus proof is possible, as it is implemented in colibri.stateless (see https://corpuscore.tech) <etan_status> higher gas cost, compared to status quo <etan_status> "there could be optimizations to make it more efficient" -> due to this, essentially <stkux> re: **@etan_status** > higher gas cost, compared to status quo What gas costs? This doesn't effect any cost on chain. Of course, generating the proofs is more effort on the RPC side (btw. we have different modi for that: 1. local prover - data is read from RPC and the proofs are generated locally and more RPC requests (e.g., for eth_getProof, data from beacon chain for consensus proof) are needed. Also, there are restriction with historical data. 2. prover service - the data is read from RPC and the proofs are provided by prover services (still fully trustless) - which is more performant and no restrictions with historical data 3. vRPC (verifiable RPC) - Data and proofs are provided by the RPC provider -> RPC becomes trustless. So, yes, it is more data read from the RPC which might consume a little bit more request tokens. Also, the latency for generating the proofs will add to the RPC's latency, but this is in the milliseconds area... <etan_status> if the 1/1 signer itself is compromised, it can just be patched to.. ignore the proofs <stkux> re: **@etan_status** > if the 1/1 signer itself is compromised, it can just be patched to.. ignore the proofs If the signer is compromised, it can ignore proofs - or could do anything else. What we solve with stateless clients is NOT that an app can't be compromised but that an app must not trust any data it receives from data providers. So, the app can't be tricked by manipulated data. <etan_status> ... unless the contract accepting the sig itself contains the LC verifier, which, today, is unnecessarily inefficient <etan_status> I agree with you, though, that colibri/helios/nimbus on the RPC client side always is better than not having it 🙂 would have at least caught that the local geth is compromised

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<stkux> re: **@etan_status**
> higher gas cost, compared to status quo
What gas costs? This doesn't effect any cost on chain. Of course, generating the proofs is more effort on the RPC side (btw. we have different modi for that: 
1. local prover - data is read from RPC and the proofs are generated locally and more RPC requests (e.g., for eth_getProof, data from beacon chain for consensus proof) are needed. Also, there are restriction with historical data.
2. prover service -  the data is read from RPC and the proofs are provided by prover services (still fully trustless) - which is more performant and no restrictions with historical data
3. vRPC (verifiable RPC) - Data and proofs are provided by the RPC provider -> RPC becomes trustless.

So, yes, it is more data read from the RPC which might consume a little bit more request tokens. Also, the latency for generating the proofs will add to the RPC's latency, but this is in the milliseconds area...

<stkux> re: **@etan_status**
> if the 1/1 signer itself is compromised, it can just be patched to.. ignore the proofs
If the signer is compromised, it can ignore proofs - or could do anything else. 
What we solve with stateless clients is NOT that an app can't be compromised but that an app must not trust any data it receives from data providers. So, the app can't be tricked by manipulated data.
